current: a limited number of hereditary peers remain following reform, and a group of Church of England bishops sit as the Lords Spiritual.
corrected: the remaining hereditary peers lost the right to sit in 2026, and a group of Church of England bishops sit as the Lords Spiritual.
reason: The House of Lords (Hereditary Peers) Act 2026 (c. 12) received Royal Assent on 18 March 2026 and removed the right of hereditary peers to sit and vote in the House of Lords when the 2024-26 session ended on 29 April 2026. The House now consists only of life peers and the Lords Spiritual, so the present-tense claim that hereditary peers remain is false. Corroborated by two independently worded searches surfacing the House of Lords Library, the House of Commons Library and legislation.gov.uk; pages not fetchable (egress blocked).
